prize_parts.citation: For foundational contributions to the theory of nominal rigidities and monetary policy rules, which underpin the microfounded analysis of monetary policy.

statement.case_for: My preferred part is unchanged, but I hold it with less confidence than in round 1. The case rests on the record and not on how many colleagues rank it. Calvo's time-dependent pricing, Taylor's staggered contracts and policy rule, and Woodford's welfare-based synthesis are dated, separately identifiable contributions. Together they form the common language in which monetary policy is analysed in academia and in central banks. The framework has been extended with financial frictions and household heterogeneity without losing its core logic of nominal rigidity plus rule-based policy. That is evidence of usefulness and adaptability. It is not, on its own, confirmation of each credited building block, and Friberg's round-1 distinction is correct on this. The chair asked what the committee should require of theory-led work. My standard, applied equally to B015, B038, B050 and B021, has three parts. The mechanism must have become the organising structure of later empirical and policy work. The credited names must map onto identifiable originating contributions. The citation must claim only what the record supports. B015 clearly meets the first test. It meets the second only with an explicit origin-plus-synthesis definition of the discovery. It meets the third only if the citation is worded around the theory of nominal rigidities and policy rules, and not around the empirical performance of the simple model after 2008 or 2021-23. Under that wording I still judge B015 the largest scientific contribution on the shortlist. I treat its earlier-prize overlap (expectations, time consistency, policy rules) as a prize-design question, not a merit question, and I would apply to it the same test of distinct incremental contribution that B038 faces against the 2008 prize. What changed in round 2 is my alternatives. I replace B016 with B050. B016 drew no explicit support in round 1 and has no attribution advantage. The B050 exchange showed a cleanly attributed, mature mechanism that deserves to be the fallback if the committee weights attribution above breadth.
statement.case_against: The attribution cost is real and I do not think it can be argued away. Eight names are credited, and Galí, Gertler, Christiano, Eichenbaum and Smets are left out. The credit for making the framework estimated and policy-ready sits outside the trio. Calvo's and Taylor's key papers predate the synthesis by about two decades, so the trio spans four decades. Earlier recognition of related work, which I know only from general knowledge, may also leave open how much of the staggered-contract idea is credited elsewhere. Calvo pricing is better read as a tractable device than as an empirical finding, and micro evidence on time- versus state-dependent adjustment is mixed. The simple representative-agent model did not clearly anticipate the 2008 financial frictions or the 2021-23 inflation dynamics. B038 and B050 have cleaner credit sets. If the committee puts attribution clarity above breadth of influence, a reasonable member could rank either above B015, and the round-1 discussion has not given me a reason to say that ordering is wrong.

responses.point: Persistence of a workhorse framework through 2008 and 2021-23 is evidence that it is useful and adaptable. It is weaker evidence that the specific building blocks credited to three people were confirmed. The citation has to be settled before the three-name set stops looking arbitrary. Calvo pricing is a tractable device, and the micro evidence on price adjustment is mixed.
responses.response: I accept the distinction and have reduced the weight I put on survival through 2008 and 2021-23. What those episodes show is that nominal rigidity and rule-based policy remain the organising structure. They do not show that Calvo's pricing rule is literally correct. I would meet your citation point by defining the discovery as the theory of nominal rigidities and policy rules, with Calvo as an originating device and Taylor as the origin of contracts and the rule. The citation would not claim empirical confirmation of Calvo pricing. The monetary non-neutrality evidence, and the estimation work that identifies it, belongs largely to the later phase, and I admit that part of the credit has no home in my trio. If the committee thinks a citation worded this way is too thin, that is an argument for preferring B038.

responses.point: Kiyotaki and Moore are a clean two-name attribution to a single 1997 paper. The financial-accelerator line is partly covered by the 2022 prize and Gertler should not be added. Direct identification of the collateral-amplification channel is mixed. B015 is his main alternative, and he would not oppose it if the credit question is settled.
responses.response: I agree that the attribution is cleaner than in B015, and I have moved B050 into my alternatives. I would apply your identification caveat symmetrically. The original collateral channel is theory-led with mixed direct tests, and B015's simple model has its own open empirical questions after 2021. On the 2022 overlap, I read it as thematic and not as a duplication of the discovery. The collateral-constraint cycle is a distinct mechanism from banks, runs and the Depression. I would keep it out of the case against even the two-name set. Where we still differ is on weight. I count B015's influence on the conduct of policy, as well as on research, a little more than the clean credit set, but I accept that this is a judgement about prize design and not something the record settles.

responses.point: The omission cost in B015 is largest on the estimation side, where Christiano-Eichenbaum-Evans and Smets-Wouters made the framework fit the data. That credit has no obvious home in a Calvo-Taylor-Woodford prize, so the citation should be worded around the theory of nominal rigidities and policy rules and not around empirical validation.
responses.response: I agree on both points, and that is how I have rewritten my citation. I would add that this makes the prize a recognition of the theoretical foundations, with the estimation phase left for the committee to consider separately. I do not think the three-name cap lets us represent the estimation phase without displacing an originator. If colleagues think the empirical turn is the central achievement, Galí replacing Calvo is the defensible variant, and I would not call it a mistake. My preference for Calvo is a judgement about originality over development.

responses.point: Dispersed credit makes B015 hard to define. His own Woodford-Galí-Gertler trio and the chair's Woodford-Taylor-Calvo trio rest on different readings of the discovery, and Gertler's presence on two ballots blurs the allocation. B038 is a better-defined single discovery with a clean credit set. He treats B015 as an alternative, not as his preferred part.
responses.response: I agree that Gertler's presence on B015 and B050 argues against building a trio around him, and I agree the two trios reflect different readings of the discovery. I still prefer the origin-plus-synthesis reading, because it is easier to state precisely who established which idea. I would not accept that dispersed credit lowers the scientific weight. It does raise the burden on the citation. Your point that B038 is cleaner as a single discovery is strong, and it is the main reason I keep B038 as my first alternative. I note that you and I are long-standing co-authors, so you should read my reply as disclosure and not as independent confirmation of anything.

uncertainties: Whether the committee will define B015 as the origin of the building blocks plus the synthesis, or as the canonical estimated model, and whether Calvo or Galí is the better third name.
How much the post-2021 inflation episode and the heterogeneous-agent critique should count against the standing of the simple framework, as against the nominal-rigidity core.

Whether earlier prizes on expectations, time consistency and policy rules reduce B015's incremental case by more than the 2008 trade prize reduces B038's. I have applied the same standard to both and have not resolved it.
Whether the committee should put attribution clarity above breadth of influence. If it does, B038 or B050 could reasonably outrank B015.
Whether a citation worded around theory and policy rules is substantive enough, given that much of the empirical confirmation belongs to contributors outside the trio.
My assessments rest on general knowledge and the supplied evidence, not on independent verification of the scientific record.
statement.conflict_note: Nothing in my supplied profile connects me to Woodford, Taylor or Calvo. The profile does show long-term co-authorship and IIES ties with John Hassler (chair), who prefers the same trio, and co-authorship with Timo Boppart (co-opted member), who discusses B015 and other ballots. Hassler's and my agreement is not independent evidence, and I disclose these ties without adjudicating them. My own research in heterogeneous-agent macroeconomics could bias me for or against a representative-agent framework, and I have tried to apply the same criteria across fields. In round 1 I mentioned an institutional tie to Torsten Persson. My supplied profile does not establish it, so I treat it as unverified, and I do not rely on it or put B021 in my preferred part or my alternatives. I have no profile-listed tie to the credited names on B038 or B050.
